extraction.primary_diagnosis: Severe menometrorrhagia unresponsive to medical therapy

primary_diagnosis_source.text: 1. Severe menometrorrhagia unresponsive to medical therapy.

source.text: Motrin 600 mg tablets 1 tablet p.o. q.8h. p.r.n. pain,
Colace 100 mg tablets 1 tablet p.o. daily p.r.n. constipation
ferrous sulfate 60 mg tablets 1 tablet p.o. daily,
and multiple vitamin 1 tablet p.o. daily.
The patient is to return on Wednesday 6/17/2009 for removal of staples.

activity_restrictions: slow return to normal activity over the ensuing 4 to 6 weeks

diagnosis_explanation:
Your primary diagnosis is heavy uterine bleeding. This bleeding was severe. It did not get better with medicine.

You also have severe anemia. This means you have a low red blood cell count. It can make you feel tired.

You have fibroids in your uterus. These are growths. They caused you to have symptoms.

You also have adenomyosis. This is a condition where the uterine lining grows into the muscle wall of the uterus. This was found after a test.
medication_rationale:
Motrin 600 mg q.8h. as needed pain:
This medicine helps ease pain and reduce swelling. It can help with cramps you may feel. You might notice some mild stomach upset. This is common and usually goes away. Call your doctor if you have black, tarry stools or severe stomach pain.

Colace 100 mg daily as needed constipation:
This medicine helps soften your stools. It makes bowel movements easier. You should notice you can go to the bathroom more easily. This means the medicine is working. Call your doctor if you have rectal bleeding or no bowel movement for three days.

Ferrous Sulfate 60 mg daily:
This medicine gives you iron. You may be low on iron because of heavy bleeding. Taking this medicine helps build your iron levels back up. Your stools may turn dark or black. This is normal and not a concern. Call your doctor if you feel very sick to your stomach or have bad constipation.

Multiple Vitamin daily:
This medicine gives you vitamins and minerals. It helps your body stay healthy. You should not notice any specific feelings from this medicine. It just helps support your overall health. Call your doctor if you have any new rash or trouble breathing.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Bleeding that will not stop: This could be life-threatening.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- You cannot keep fluids down: You may get too dry.
- Feeling very weak or dizzy: You may need blood now.
- Bad pelvic pain that worsens: This could mean bleeding inside.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about your iron pills: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Mild bleeding that slows down: This can happen while you heal.
- Feeling tired but not worse: This is normal for now.
